name: Tamsin Velle
summary: A hydroponics shift lead and unofficial station listener who trades in small comforts and small truths, collecting what people won’t write down because it sounds like fear.

role_in_world.scope: Crop schedules, vault maintenance coordination, informal conflict mediation

flaws: can become protective to a fault

beliefs: People will endure anything if they feel seen.
Systems fail where humans stop talking to each other.
The station’s public calm is paid for with private worry.
blind_spots: Sometimes procedure exists for a reason.
Information can become a weapon even when shared kindly.

voice.speech_style: plainspoken, tactile, uses plant and food metaphors despite herself
tells: asks 'how are you sleeping?' as a diagnostic
offers something small before asking something hard
keeps her tone gentle while her questions cut clean
sample_lines: You can tell a lot from what people stop seasoning.
If the air tastes different, don’t let anyone tell you it’s imagination.

pressures: Crop schedules are tightening 'for efficiency' and nobody will say why.
A technician quietly warns her about seals, and she doesn’t know what to do with the warning.
Community morale is slipping in small ways: jokes thinning, silences lengthening.

secrets_and_fears.fear: A slow failure will be normalized until it becomes irreversible.
secrets_and_fears.secret: Tamsin keeps an off-record ledger of 'air taste' and 'sleep quality' reports from residents, because the dashboards don’t track those.

story_hooks: Tamsin hears the phrase '17-B' from two unrelated people in the same day.
During the Lantern Walk, a child asks why the end-silence is longer this year.
A hydroponics vault shows subtle stress that looks like nutrient drift, but feels like something else.
